5 تلغّب : see 4. ―
-b2- He chased, hunted, or pursued, long: syn. of the inf. n. طُولُ الطَّرْدِ. (S, K.) ―
-b3- A poet says, “تَلَغَّبَنِى دَهْرٌ فَلَمَّا غَلَبْتُهُ
غَزَانِى بِأَوْلَادِى فَأَدْرَكَنِى الدَّهْرُ
” [Fortune long pursued me; and when I overcame him, he attacked me with my children; and so fortune overtook me]. (S.) ―
-b4- تلغّبهُ He undertook the management of it, and did it, and was not unequal to it. (TA.) ―
-b5- تلغّب الدَّابَّةَ He found the beast of carriage to be fatigued, tired, or weary; or so in the utmost degree. (TA.) See 2.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
